checklist.heading: Setup checklist
checklist.blurb: Keep the workspace basics configured before the team starts planning.

lifecycle.label: Pick a workspace timezone
lifecycle.unconfiguredBlurb: Defaults to UTC; pick the team's timezone so lead-time math matches the calendar.

monthlyTarget.label: Set a monthly content target
monthlyTarget.unconfiguredBlurb: The planning KPI bar colours on-track / at-risk / off-track against this number.

leadTimes.label: Tune the lead-time buffers
leadTimes.configuredBlurb: Lead times are at the 10/5/2/1 default — adjust to match your team's cadence.

defaults.label: Set default assignees
defaults.configuredBlurb: All four roles have a default assignee.
defaults.unconfiguredBlurb: {count} of 4 roles have a default assignee.

bulkReset.title: Reset all ideas
bulkReset.blurb: Platform-only. Archive every idea in this workspace and zero the counters. Action is undoable for {hours} hours.
bulkReset.confirm: Type the workspace name to confirm.
bulkReset.dialogTitle: Reset every idea in this workspace
bulkReset.dialogBody: Permanently deletes every idea in {name} plus all 8 cascade children. Workspace settings, channels, the brand kit, and other workspaces in the agency are not affected.
bulkReset.countsPreview: {count} ideas will be deleted ({excluded} live ideas skipped because 'Include published' is off).
bulkReset.includePublishedHint: Off by default. When ON, also deletes ideas in published and partially_published status. Those ideas have at least one live post on a social network — deleting them here removes the LaraTik record, but the public post is not retracted.
bulkReset.liveWarning: You are about to delete {count} live ideas. The LaraTik record will be gone; any public social posts will remain unless you retract them separately.
bulkReset.typedPhraseLabel: Type the workspace's name to confirm
bulkReset.reasonHelp: At least 8 characters. Saved to the platform audit log alongside the full list of idea IDs that were removed.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: The workspace identity for scheduling. The timezone drives the calendar, lead-time math, and every 'X days from now' view; the monthly target is the planning KPI bar's reference.
lifecycle.readOnly: Read-only. Workspace manager access is required to edit these settings.
lifecycle.timezoneHint: Used for the calendar, lead-time math, and any 'X days from now' view.
lifecycle.monthlyTargetHint: Optional. The planning KPI bar uses this to colour on-track / at risk / off-track.
lifecycle.applied: Suggestion applied. Edit any number before saving.
lifecycle.previewBlurb: Anchored to your lead-time cycle so the team can sustain the cadence.

leadTimes.title: Lead times
leadTimes.description: Four numbers that drive every 'auto-suggest a planned date' on the planning surface. They sum to the end-to-end cycle for a normal post.
leadTimes.readOnly: Read-only. Workspace manager access is required to edit these settings.
leadTimes.contentApprovalHint: Buffer between brief approval and the designer's first-pass art.
leadTimes.designCompleteHint: Buffer between first-pass art and the creative-ready handoff.
leadTimes.creativeApprovalHint: Buffer for the internal creative reviewer (and the client, if the mode includes one).
leadTimes.readyToPublishHint: Buffer between final approval and the actual publish moment.
leadTimes.contextBody: With the current buffers, a post started today lands on the publish-ready stage on:

defaults.title: Assignment defaults
defaults.description: Pre-fills on Quick Create. Per-item overrides always win — the default is a shortcut, not a rule.
defaults.formBlurb: Pre-fill these people on every new idea. Override per idea at any time — the default is a shortcut, not a rule.
defaults.readOnly: Read-only. Workspace manager access is required to edit these settings.
defaults.designerHint: Pre-fills the designer field on the Quick Create form.
defaults.contentReviewerHint: The first-pass reviewer on the brief. Usually the content lead.
defaults.internalCreativeHint: The creative director. Only used when approval mode is 'Internal, then client'.
defaults.clientReviewerHint: The client's primary approver. Appears in the 'Client review' step.
defaults.emptyOption: No people with this role yet
defaults.currentDefault: Current default applied on new ideas.

approvals.title: Approval mode
approvals.description: How many approval steps a piece of content needs before publish.
approvals.readOnly: Read-only. Workspace manager access is required to edit these settings.
approvals.fieldHint: How many approval steps a piece of content needs before publish.

modeSimple.label: Internal approval only
modeSimple.blurb: One approver. Faster cycle. Best for in-house or single-stakeholder content.
modeSimple.days: Single-step. ~ 1-3 business days from brief to publish.

modeInternalThenClient.label: Internal, then client
modeInternalThenClient.blurb: Two approvers. Adds a client-review stage. Use when the brand has an external stakeholder.
modeInternalThenClient.days: Two-step. ~ 5-10 business days from brief to publish.

approvals.stepInternalReviewTwoHint: Content lead + creative director sign off.
approvals.stepClientReviewHint: Client approver signs off before publish-ready.
approvals.impactOk: Your current lead times look right for this mode.
approvals.impactIdle: Switch modes above to see what changes across the other settings.
approvals.impactWarnNoCreativeBuffer: Your creative_approval_lead_days is 0. The creative review step won't have a buffer; set it on the Lead times page (try 2-4 days).
approvals.impactWarnPublishShortOne: Your ready_to_publish_lead_days is 1 day. The client review cycle usually needs 3-6 days.
approvals.impactWarnPublishShortMany: Your ready_to_publish_lead_days is {count} days. The client review cycle usually needs 3-6 days.
approvals.impactWarnCreativeUnused: Your creative_approval_lead_days is {count} day(s). The simple mode has no creative review step, so this number has no effect.

templates.title: Settings presets
templates.description: Curated preset values for the four numbers every new workspace has to set. Each card shows the delta against your current settings so you can see what changes before applying.
templates.managerRequired: You need workspace-manager access to apply presets.

leadTimesSection.title: Lead time presets
leadTimesSection.blurb: Curated 4-number presets for common agency cadences. Applying a lead-time preset also adjusts the approval mode when the preset is designed for a client-approval workflow.

approvalsSection.title: Approval mode presets
approvalsSection.blurb: The two approval flows the workspace supports.

monthlyTargetSection.title: Monthly target presets
monthlyTargetSection.blurb: Common post-per-month targets the planning KPI bar uses to colour on-track / at-risk / off-track.

templates.leadClientHint: This preset flips approval mode to 'Internal, then client'.

leadFast.name: Fast (8 days)
leadFast.blurb: Lean team, daily cadence, low review depth. Use when speed > polish.

leadStandard.name: Standard (14 days)
leadStandard.blurb: Most agencies. Two weeks end-to-end. Room for the writer's first pass + a creative pass.

leadRelaxed.name: Relaxed (24 days)
leadRelaxed.blurb: Monthly cadence, deep review, multiple stakeholders. Use when quality > speed.

leadClient.name: Agency + client (22 days)
leadClient.blurb: Internal review + client review. The most common external-stakeholder workflow.

approvalSimple.blurb: One approver. Faster cycle. Best for in-house content or single-stakeholder brands.

approvalClient.blurb: Two approvers. Use when an external stakeholder signs off before publish.

monthly12.name: 3 / week
monthly12.blurb: 12 posts per month. A solid weekly cadence.

monthly20.name: 5 / week
monthly20.blurb: 20 posts per month. A common agency target.

monthly30.name: Daily
monthly30.blurb: 30 posts per month. A high-volume brand.

monthly60.name: 2 / day
monthly60.blurb: 60 posts per month. Multi-channel or always-on brand.

sectionBlurb.lifecycle: Timezone + monthly target. Used for the calendar, lead-time math, and the planning KPI bar.
sectionBlurb.lead-times: Four numbers that drive every auto-suggested planned date on the planning surface.
sectionBlurb.defaults: Pre-fills on Quick Create. Per-item overrides always win — the default is a shortcut, not a rule.
sectionBlurb.approvals: How many approval steps a piece of content needs before publish: internal only, or internal + client.

suggestions.lifecycleTimezone: Pick a workspace timezone so the calendar renders in local time.
suggestions.lifecycleMonthlyTarget: Set a monthly content target so the planning KPI bar can show on-track / at-risk / off-track.
suggestions.lifecycleLowTarget: Your target is fewer than 1 post per week. Most agencies plan against 8-24 posts per month.
suggestions.lifecycleHighTarget: A target above 60 posts / month means more than 2 posts per business day. Consider whether the team can sustain it.
suggestions.leadTimesEmpty: Set at least one lead time before planning the first post.
suggestions.leadTimesShort: Total lead time under 5 business days. Most agencies need at least 8-12 to keep quality high.
suggestions.leadTimesLong: Total lead time over 30 business days — a 6-week cycle. The planner may struggle to hit publishing windows.
suggestions.leadTimesContentShort: Content approval under 3 days. The writer may not have time to incorporate the content lead's feedback.
suggestions.leadTimesContentLong: Content approval over 14 days. The brief is sitting idle for too long before the first pass.
suggestions.leadTimesDesignShort: Design complete under 2 days. The designer is producing first-pass art in under 2 business days.
suggestions.defaultsEmpty: No default assignees yet. Every new content item will require a manual pick on the Quick Create form.
suggestions.defaultsOne: Only 1 default assignee. Plan against at least the designer + content reviewer so the team has a clear first stop.
suggestions.defaultsPartial: Most slots have a default. Add the missing slot so every role is auto-pre-filled on new items.
suggestions.defaultsHealthy: All four roles have a default assignee.
suggestions.approvalsSimple: Internal approval only. Switch to 'Internal, then client' if the brand has an external stakeholder who needs to sign off.
suggestions.approvalsClient: Internal, then client. The creative_approval + client_review stages are active.
